title: Replication, sharding, and the query that no longer fits

videos.script: There are two reasons to put data on more than one machine, and they lead to two different designs. {{two}} The first is that one machine can fail. So you keep copies, and that is replication. {{replication}} The second is that one machine is not big enough. So you split the data into pieces, and that is sharding. {{sharding}} Replication you have already met, in lesson 8. Here you will measure it: how far behind a copy is, in bytes and in seconds. {{measure}} Then a cluster of three Kafka nodes, where you stop the nodes one at a time and watch what still works. Three is not an arbitrary number, and you will see why. {{three}} Then Quitanda's orders split across two databases. Questions about one customer stay as fast as before. A question about everybody turns into something else, and the obvious way to ask it gives the wrong answer. {{wrong}} Last, adding a third database, and how many customers have to move when you do.
